-- **Inbound mail contact lookups at scale:** an inbound mail's contact lookups by address (the blocked-sender check, the sender's and each Cc's contact, the new-contact guard, and a reply's sender through a reply address or from a preferred notification address) search an index of the address instead of walking every contact of a large imported workspace, and a member reply's send issues each recipient's reply address by reading the conversation's own contact and participants by key. An ordinary inbound mail on a workspace of about 160,000 contacts reads about 1,400 rows instead of about 490,000, and the send of a reply about 180 instead of about 320,000. Every lookup matches exactly the contacts it matched before. Apply `322_contact_address_lookup.sql` after 321.
-- **Fixes — conversations whose text repeats help-site passages no longer overload D1:** in a large imported workspace whose crawled help site shares boilerplate across hundreds of pages, a conversation open, thread read, inbox list or search, inbound mail or member reply whose text repeats such passages evaluated the knowledge reference policy once per (passage, reader, page) occurrence, and looked up each page's current version by walking the whole published version: over a million D1 rows per evaluation, several evaluations per open, and `503` once opens came in a row. The policy now decides each passage for each reader with one search that stops at the first page that decides it, and a page of the published version is its own current page, so a 16-passage open reads over a hundred times fewer rows. What each reader is shown, and what admission and outbound mail allow, is unchanged. One limit remains: on a very large imported desk whose older crawl version's documents no longer have their URLs, one evaluation can still read many rows until the planned index for older crawl versions exists, and this release does not remove that. Our recommendation to operators: keep mail off on a host with imported help documents until further notice.
-- **Fixes — the help-article `500` reached back to v0.4.15:** the knowledge reference policy code that real D1 refuses was byte-identical in v0.4.15, v0.4.16 and v0.4.17 and unchanged in v0.4.18, so an installation of any of them with published help articles answered `500` when a member opened, or searched the inbox for, a conversation whose text overlaps an article, and on inbound mail that quotes one. v0.4.19 fixed it and this release keeps that fix; the v0.4.19 notes named only v0.4.17 and v0.4.18.
-- **Erasing a teammate retires them from the Business roster:** erasing a teammate account now also removes them from the roster their Business signed: their team row and their entry in the stored Business settings document are removed in the same transaction as the erasure, their policy references in local agent policy are retired the same way, and only a value-free tombstone (digests of the roster address and Business member id with the invite number they had) is kept. The Business's next signed revision that still lists an erased teammate applies as retired: every other value and teammate applies, and the erased person gets no account, no invitation and no row until the Business sends a larger invite number. Before, a signed revision listing an erased teammate was refused with `member_erased` and the person's hash-named roster row and renamed document entry stayed. A teammate erased by an earlier release leaves the roster at the Business's next revision, listed or not. Adopts rer 0.2.107 and its Base copy. One corner remains, in Base's `retireGone` handling: a teammate erased by v0.4.19 or an earlier release and left unlisted by the Business, then listed by a later revision at the same invite number with their real address and no member id, can get a fresh account and an invitation where the earlier release refused with `member_erased`; a Business that sends member ids is fully fenced, and Base tracks this as a follow-up.
-- **Fixes — `rer deploy` names the mail secrets:** the deployment declaration now lists the seven outbound-mail secret names (`EMAIL_PROVIDER`, `EMAIL_FROM`, `EMAIL_API_KEY_NAME`, `MAILGUN_DOMAIN`, `MAILGUN_REGION`, `MAILGUN_SENDING_KEY`, `MAILGUN_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY`), so `rer deploy` prints one line naming the mail secrets bound on the Worker instead of the false "Outbound email is off"; an offline `rer deploy --dry-run` lists the seven names and says the bound secrets were not read. No behaviour change for mail itself.
-- **Migrations:** `322_contact_address_lookup.sql`, `323_business_retired.sql`. Apply once, in this order, after `321_legacy_import_files.sql` and BEFORE the new Worker serves traffic. `322_contact_address_lookup.sql` is additive and creates two indexes on contacts. `323_business_retired.sql` is additive and creates one empty table, `bs_retired`; without it, erasing a teammate refuses with `business_roster_missing_table:bs_retired`.
+- **Access hardening — an owner changes a teammate's sign-in only where that workspace is the account's only one:** a teammate's password, second factors and recovery codes belong to the account, not to one workspace, but before this release an owner of any workspace the account belonged to could issue it a password-reset link or reset its two-factor sign-in, which changed how the account signs in for its other workspaces too. Now: (1) an owner's password-reset link for a teammate is issued only while that workspace holds the account's sole membership and the account does not administer the installation, otherwise it is refused with `409`, and the link names that workspace; (2) accepting such a link checks the same rule again in the write itself, so a link whose account has since joined another workspace is refused (`409`, "This reset link no longer applies") and spends nothing; (3) an owner's two-factor reset for a teammate (their factors and recovery codes removed, their sessions ended) is refused with `409` for an account that also belongs to another workspace or administers the installation, and its three deletions carry the same condition; (4) the reset link an account holder requests by email (`forgot-password`) now belongs to the account and names no workspace, so it is not tied to this rule. An account that also belongs to another workspace changes its own sign-in. Invitation links are unchanged: the shared token check that invitation acceptance uses carries the reset rule for reset links only. An unused reset link issued by v0.4.20 or earlier for an account that belongs to more than one workspace, or administers the installation, is refused after the upgrade: request a new one by email. No migration and no data step: deploy the new Worker.
+- **Known limit — the roster corner for teammates erased by v0.4.19 or earlier is wider than the v0.4.20 notes said:** a Business that keeps listing an erased teammate by real address without a member id gets the same re-creation one revision later, and the first such revision keeps their name and address in the stored Business settings; the code fix is a Base round (gr-base-roster-corner-1). A Business that sends member ids is fenced.
+- **Migrations:** No migrations since v0.4.20. v0.4.21 adds no migration file, so a v0.4.20 installation's migration ledger stays unchanged.
